auditTrail.issue: An earlier snapshot labeled the FY25/FY24 standalone operating cash flow values (₹4,225 crore/₹3,449.7 crore) as consolidated.
auditTrail.correction: Rechecked the official FY2024-25 annual report consolidated Ind AS cash-flow statement: the operating cash flow row is on printed p. 351 (PDF p. 177), ₹46,428 million/₹45,433 million, converted to ₹4,642.8 crore/₹4,543.3 crore by dividing by 10.

auditTrail.note: The KPI summary on PDF p. 6 reports PBT of ₹76,784 million; the separate consolidated Ind AS Board Report table at printed pp. 92-93 reports ₹76,795 million. These are distinct source presentations, so QA records the app’s chosen metric and citation basis rather than treating one figure as universally incorrect.

claimCitations.claim: FY26 EBITDA rose 13.4% to ₹2,07,911 crore and PAT 17.8% to ₹95,754 crore, led by Digital Services and O2C.
Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA was a record ₹62,409 crore, up 24% year on year, with PAT up 34%.
Retail EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% from 8.6% in FY26.
Management cited currency depreciation, a monsoon deficit and food inflation weighing on discretionary demand, and margin pressure from matching quick-commerce prices.
Gross NPA ratio improved to 1.15% from 1.33%, and cost-to-income fell to 38.0% from 40.5%.
Q2 FY27 deposits grew 18.8% year on year, about 4 points of it from a special FCNR(B) window; CASA grew about 10.8%.
Net interest income grew only 4.9% in FY26, much slower than net revenues, which were lifted by other income.
Management said margins had absorbed faster asset repricing and a lag in funding costs; a new leader is yet to set out strategy.
NII grew 8.5% to ₹880.75 billion with NIM stable at 4.32%.
Q1 FY27 PAT grew 15.9% to ₹148.05 billion and deposits 14.0% year on year.
FY26 standalone PAT grew 6.2%, slower than NII.
The credit-card portfolio declined 1.9% year on year and 1.7% sequentially in Q1 FY27.
FY26 net profit rose 12.88% to ₹80,032 crore; RoA improved to 1.12% and RoE was 18.57%.
Q2 FY27 net profit was ₹23,038 crore and domestic NIM improved to 3.11%; H1 RoE was 18.68%.
Net interest income grew only 4.08% in FY26.
Q2 FY27 operating profit growth slowed to 7.28% year on year.
FY26 operating margin of 25.0% and net margin of 19.8% were the highest in four years; net income grew 8.8%.
All international markets grew sequentially in Q2 FY27, led by the UK at 3.5%.
FY26 revenue grew only 4.6%.
Management described the environment as selective and uneven, and cited bench and subcontractor costs as headwinds; it gives no guidance.
FY26 consolidated revenue grew 9.6% to ₹1,78,650 crore.
Q2 FY27 operating margin was stable at 21% with free cash flow of US$928 million.
PBT grew only 6.3% after a ₹1,289 crore labour-code exceptional charge.
FY27 revenue guidance is 1%-2% in constant currency; management saw weakness in retail and hi-tech.
Q2 FY27 operating margin improved 0.5 points to 16.5%, and three of four market units grew sequentially.
Standalone net profit grew 11.15% in FY26.
Consolidated net profit grew only 0.36% in FY26 on 3.97% sales growth.
Q3 FY27 guidance is -1.5% to +0.5% sequential growth; US healthcare is affected by policy changes.
FY26 consolidated revenue grew 16.2% and EBITDAaL 15.7%; India ARPU rose ₹12 to ₹257.
Q2 FY27 revenue grew 4% sequentially, Africa 6.7% in constant currency, with a 51.7% EBITDAaL margin.
Reported PBT grew only 2.1% because FY25 included exceptional gains; tax expense rose sharply to ₹11,350 crore.
Management said cost pressures are building and growth funding depends on its War on Waste cost programme.
FY26 order inflow rose 22% to ₹4.36 lakh crore and the order book 28% to ₹7.40 lakh crore.
Q1 FY27 group order inflow grew 14% to ₹1,080 billion.
Reported consolidated PAT grew 7.0%, well below the 18% recurring PAT growth the company highlights.
Domestic order inflow grew only 1% in Q1 FY27, versus 27% internationally.
FY26 gross revenue grew 10.1% to ₹80,867 crore; the cigarettes segment grew through differentiated and premium offerings.
EBITDA grew only 4.9% and PAT 1.0%, well below revenue growth.
Quarterly USG improved from 3% in H1 FY26 to 7% in the March quarter.
Q2 FY27 USG was 15%, the highest in 14 quarters, with 7% UVG.
FY26 turnover grew only 5% with 4% volume growth.
Inflation softened mass tea performance; Foods volume growth was low single digit.
FY26 revenue grew 17.4% and PAT 20.5%, with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 20.5%.
Exports rose to about 7.5 lakh units a quarter from 6 lakh last year, and management expects to sustain it.
Management cited inflationary pressures, logistics complexity and capacity limits for high-end bikes, exports and EVs.
Q2 FY27 sales volume was a record 696,654 units, up 26.5%, with pending orders around 2 lakh units.
FY26 standalone PBT fell to ₹188,629 million from ₹194,127 million despite higher income.
Q2 FY27 exports fell about 2% on logistics disruption; management gives no guidance and flagged commodity risk in H2.
Consolidated revenue grew 11.2% and pre-exceptional PBT 13.8% in FY26.
Q2 FY27 India sales grew 17.3% and market share rose to 8.6% from 8.3%.
A ₹1,307 crore exceptional item cut PAT growth to 5.3%; standalone revenue fell to ₹207,546 million from ₹229,774 million.
R&D spend was tracking below plan, with management expecting H2 to catch up, which may weigh on H2 margins.
Consolidated PAT reached a record ₹27,546 crore, up 15%, and group capacity rose 11.48% to 89,108 MW.
India power demand grew about 15% in H1 FY27, with October up 21%.
Profit from group companies fell 2.78% because FY25 included one-time revenue at RGPPL.
Renewable capacity guidance was cut because of transmission constraints.
FY26 consolidated EBITDA grew 11.2% to ₹16,090 crore and PAT 7.2% to ₹5,118 crore.
Q1 FY27 PAT grew 11% to ₹1,401 crore and EBITDA 8% to ₹4,249 crore.
Finance costs rose to ₹5,257 crore from ₹4,702 crore, and standalone PAT fell to ₹1,125 crore from ₹3,133 crore.
FY26 consolidated EBITDA grew 12.78% and PBT 17.64% on revenue growth of 4.95%.
Q2 FY27 decorative volume grew 6.4% and value 14.5%.
Revenue grew under 5% in FY26.
Much of Q2 FY27 value growth came from price increases rather than volume.
FY26 consolidated revenue (+15%) and EBITDA (+7%) were records, led by India operations.
Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 52% to ₹13,869 crore and PAT 59% to ₹7,533 crore.
The Oswego fire and higher US tariffs hurt Novelis shipments and FY26 margins.
Q2 copper EBITDA included one-time gains, and management flagged geopolitical, commodity and trade headwinds.
FY25 AUM grew 26%, net total income 24%, and PAT 16%; the customer franchise reached 101.82 million.
Loan-loss provisions increased 72%; management cited macro deterioration, leverage in unsecured loans and rising banking-sector stress.

FY25 consolidated revenue rose 18.4%; the issuer EBITDA-equivalent line item rose 6.1%, while consolidated PBT fell 1.9% and PAT fell 4.6%. Standalone jewellery revenue excluding bullion was ₹46,571 crore.
Management continued to target high-double-digit jewellery growth.
Consolidated PBT fell 1.9% and PAT fell 4.6% in FY25.
Management described pressure in lower jewellery price bands amid gold-price uncertainty.
FY25 revenue grew 17%, EBITDA margin was 28.3%, RoCE was 27.7%, and consolidated operating cash flow increased year over year.
PAT attributable to equity holders rose only 2%; the annual report says all three internal scorecard pillars were below plan.
